messages:
Luca: Heads-up — after we pushed NCCL 2.24.2 to the canary A100 pool in us-west3 we're seeing multi-GPU inference jobs hang and large tail-latency spikes (~20-40%). A few jobs stuck in allreduce for >30s. Can we pause the rest of the rollout? :eyes:

Ayesha: Noted. Which node image/kernel are the canary hosts on? Any obvious driver/CUDA mismatches?

Joel: Repro logs from one stuck pod attached below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17 14:02:12] NCCL INFO rank 1 -> allgather start
[2026-03-17 14:02:42] NCCL WARN Timeout waiting for remote op, last active rank 2
[2026-03-17 14:02:42] NCCL ERROR Allreduce timeout on comm 0x7f9b4c
[2026-03-17 14:03:10] GPU0: kernel launch error: unspecified launch failure
```
Pods with single-GPU tasks are fine. Multi-GPU (4x A100 nvlink) are affected intermittently.

Kai: Canary nodes are on ubuntu-20.04 + driver 525.85 + CUDA 11.8. We did bump kernel from 5.10->5.15 last week but that was in a separate rollout (should be stable). NCCL 2.24.2 was the only change this morning.

sre-oncall: Impact — ~12% of production multi-gpu inferences failing in us-west3, increased 99p latency by ~3.2x. Please pause and rollback if safe. Raising incident INC-20260317-01.

deploy-bot: canary deployment: nccl=2.24.2 -> applied to pool 'canary-a100-us-west3' at 2026-03-17T14:00:02Z

Luca: Agreed — pause rollout and rollback the canary to 2.23.1. Joel, can you collect a minimized repro (container + mpirun config)? ops, can you hold capacity for a rollback window? :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Suggested quick repro to run on a canary node:
```
# run on 4 GPUs
mpirun -np 4 -bind-to none -map-by slot -x NCCL_DEBUG=INFO \
  -x CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 python3 tests/collective_perf.py --model gpt-medium-quant --batch 1 --seq 1024
```
If it hangs consistently please save /var/log/nccl.log and dmesg.

Joel: Pushed rollback to canary pool now. Rolling to 2.23.1. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: pool 'canary-a100-us-west3' nccl=2.24.2 -> nccl=2.23.1 at 2026-03-17T14:07:55Z

Ayesha: Quick mitigation idea — set NCCL_TIMEOUT to 250000 or disable collective autotune on affected services while we root cause. Might avoid user-visible hangs.

Luca: Apply NCCL_TIMEOUT env on the inference deployment for canary traffic split (20%) and route rest to dedicated unaffected pools. I'll coordinate with traffic-split in the console.

Joel: Rollback complete. Early metrics look good — 99p latency back to baseline and no hangs for the last 10 minutes. Will attach traces and perf diffs to the incident.

sre-oncall: Thanks. Keep follow-up with NVIDIA / NCCL upstream. We should add a preflight collectives smoke to the nccl upgrade playbook (short mpirun allreduce test on nvlink topology).

Luca: Agreed. I'll open a short RFC for an automated canary smoke and add it to the release checklist. Closing incident once postmortem is written. :white_check_mark:
